questionText: A black square PQRS has been cut into two parts. One part of it is shown in Panel I. Which one of the shapes in Panel II is the other part?
explanation:
Step 1: Understand the requirement.
A solid black square $PQRS$ has been split into two complementary pieces. Panel I displays one piece, where the white region represents the missing shape required to complete the square.

Step 2: Analyze the white region in Panel I.
The required piece must perfectly fill the white space in Panel I without any overlap or missing segments.

Step 3: Match with Panel II shapes.
Comparing the geometry, orientation, and interlocking projections of the white cutout with the figures in Panel II, shape (iii) corresponds exactly to the missing piece.
